title: AidSight
summary: A privacy-first guide that helps people find real aid programs by reachability—not merely by whether help technically exists.
problem: Food, shelter, legal help, health care, capital, and residencies exist, yet the people they were built for often cannot find or safely evaluate them.
scope: Product concept, verified research system, three design directions, interaction design, and a self-contained static implementation.
approach: Grade programs by practical reachability, from show-up-and-get-help to chronically waitlisted.
Run a second research pass against every cited official source and expose claim checks in the interface.
Keep search and filtering on-device so sensitive queries never leave the page.
outcome: A public, browsable MVP with an intake wizard, source-level evidence, explicit limitations, and three comparable design systems. No adoption or impact result is claimed yet.
limits: The dataset is a July 2026 snapshot, is primarily US-focused, and must be confirmed against each official source before someone acts.

title: Naked Health
summary: A branded web-and-mobile health guidance concept built around practical, culturally aware harm reduction rather than judgment.
problem: Health guidance often becomes clinical, generic, or moralizing precisely when a person needs candid, context-aware help.
scope: Brand system, responsive web experience, native mobile flows, service architecture, and a streaming conversational-guide prototype.
approach: Pair a calm editorial identity with direct, scenario-led guidance.
Design the web and native experiences as one product system with shared topics and language.
Frame the conversational guide around harm reduction and explicit limits rather than diagnosis.
outcome: A demo-quality Next.js web app and Expo mobile app that make the product, brand, and cross-platform interaction model concrete. Clinical validation and production use are not claimed.
limits: This is a concept prototype, not medical advice, a regulated clinical product, or evidence of real-world health outcomes.

title: FashionAI
summary: An early consumer-product prototype exploring playful outfit feedback, personal taste signals, inspiration, and a premium interaction model.
problem: Most digital style tools separate inspiration, feedback, and personal preference instead of learning from the full loop.
scope: Product flows and a React prototype spanning onboarding, scoring, suggestions, chat, inspiration, and subscription states.
approach: Use a quick score and a concise remark as an understandable first feedback layer.
Connect suggestions and inspiration to the preference signals gathered during onboarding.
Prototype the premium boundary as part of the product flow rather than a separate marketing screen.
outcome: A first-draft interaction model for evaluating the concept before native implementation. Model quality, customer demand, and commercial outcomes were not validated.
limits: Scores and AI feedback are mocked; the repository documents a product concept, not a production recommendation system.
